summary: Latency 'butterfly effect' from simultaneous coldstarts causing regional dedicated pool GPU scarcity
description: Issue summary: Over the afternoon window a subset of customers in the us-west dedicated cluster experienced sustained p95/p99 latency increases. Root cause appears to be a cascade triggered by many simultaneous coldstart requests for long-context chat sessions. The resulting scheduling heartbeats and heavy prefetch work overloaded GPU attach paths and NVMe IO, leading to short-term GPU scarcity and degraded throughput across the pool.
impact: Multiple dedicated customers (including BrightInsight Analytics) saw p95 increase from ~280ms to >1.6s and p99 spikes above 4s for generation endpoints. Throughput dropped by ~22% in the affected stripe during the 14:05-14:35 window. No data loss; higher latencies caused request timeouts for some customer clients and elevated error rates in application-layer retries.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Create many simultaneous coldstart chat streams targeting long-context (8k+) model variants.
2) Ensure clients hold open keepalive and send initial messages that trigger KV prefetch for long contexts.
3) Rapidly scale the fanout to 150-200 short-lived streams per tenant in the same regional stripe.
4) Observe autoscaler fairness and attach latency under load; monitor GPU attach latency and scheduler queue length.
logs: 14:06:03 prefetcher: kv_prefetch_io_bytes spike to 1.8GB/s on nvme-0
14:07:20 autoscaler: scale_decision delayed=37s due to telemetry gap
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: standard noisy-tenant batcher. Rejected after per-tenant throughput showed many tenants simultaneously initiating coldstarts.
Telemetry shows correlated spikes in NVMe io and scheduler attach latency coincident with keepalive-heavy short-lived streams.
Autoscaler telemetry ingestion lag (obsd in 14:06 window) caused it to defer allocations; smoothing thresholds then suppressed immediate burst scaling.
Prefetcher aggressively populated long-context KV caches for each coldstart without backoff, amplifying NVMe pressure and HBM usage on select GPUs, which created temporary attach blocking.
We observed degraded fairness: quick-stream tenants consumed ephemeral allocator credits leading to GPU slot fragmentation.
Cross-referenced with SUP-712909 and SUP-421800 - similar coldstart-prefetch interactions but different cluster topology.
comments: Support (Aisha): Customer reports emerged at 14:12 — initial remediation attempted: route to fallback variant (lower-context) for affected customers; helped reduce p99 but not p95.
SRE (Marco): Rolled a temporary autoscaler smoothing override at 14:22 to force +2 nodes in stripe; attach latencies improved over next 6 minutes.
Customer (BrightInsight - Sarah W.): Confirmed latency improvement after fallback routing and requested permanent fix/controls to prevent future multi-tenant coldstart storms.
Eng (Liu Chen): Identified prefetcher without per-tenant prefetch backoff as amplification factor; PR drafted to introduce exponential backoff and aggregate prefetch batching.
root_cause: Simultaneous coldstarts from multiple tenants triggered aggressive per-stream KV prefetch on long-context variants. That amplified NVMe IO and HBM pressure, which increased scheduler attach latency. A telemetry ingestion lag caused the autoscaler to delay scale-up, creating a temporary GPU scarcity (noisy-butterfly effect) that reduced throughput and raised tail latency across the stripe.
resolution_notes: Mitigation applied: 1) Short-term: forced capacity (+2 nodes) to the stripe and enabled routing-based fallback to lower-context model variants for affected customers. 2) Mid-term: deployed autoscaler telemetry ingestion fix and temporary lowering of smoothing windows to react faster to coldstart waves. 3) Code change: prefetcher PR (see related PR) to add per-tenant exponential backoff and aggregate prefetch windows to reduce NVMe burstiness.
Customer-facing resolution: Customer's requests were routed to lower-context fallback for 40 minutes, then gradually reintroduced to normal model; observed p95 back to baseline ~14:40.
Status: Partial fix merged to canary; full rollout scheduled after smoke tests.
next_steps: 1) Complete code review and merge prefetch backoff PR; schedule rollout to canary and then prod (owner: Liu Chen).
2) Add an autoscaler test to simulate high-coldstart fanout and validate smoothing thresholds (owner: Marco Reyes).
3) Improve dedicated-pool telemetry alerts for NVMe io spikes and attach latency (owner: Observability team).
4) Follow up with BrightInsight on SLA credits and optional model-pin controls to avoid fallback in future (owner: CS manager).
resolution: In progress - temporary mitigations applied; code fix in review
